name: Bonded-Store Slip
notes: An East Empire Company storekeeper at Soulrest. The slip lies in the salvage at Chasepoint, 355 m from Soulrest; the Company is gone from the province and its bonded stores are not. Saltrice, the Archon line and the stores at Soulrest are dossier fact. The year 4E 31, the quantity and the charge are the slip's own particulars.

name: Carriage Charge Ledger
notes: The tag-keeper of the Tag House, who receives the fee and writes every payment in the ledger. The families of the Rose release the dead for a carriage charge and the Chainbreakers pay it; the bones must reach the dirt. Names, tag numbers and sums are the keeper's own entries.

name: Column Pay Book
notes: The column's clerk, in the command tent of the Broke Column: the last page of the pay book that the camp's current men keep as an inheritance. The record says part of the column deserted at the recall, about two centuries before 4E 201. The Legion never paid them; the catalogue provenance is 'the pay book, with the last entry in it'. The recall at 3E 433 follows the Oblivion Crisis row; the arrears counts are the clerk's own entries. The text names no payer, so it does not settle FG07's 'who pays'.

name: Depth Sticks and Dried Buds
notes: Written by a river guide for the road trade and sold at Claywater Station to travellers who will not hire a guide. The depth stick and buds are the water kit named in the fauna dossier. The length of the stick and the waiting before drinking are the writer's own practice, not dossier fact.

name: Duty Roster
notes: The clerk of the Broke Column, in a clerk's hand, nailed to the aspen in the palisade gap below the tents. The serjeant's name is from npcs.json (npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1); the men, posts and watches are the clerk's entries. The record: the men keep watches, wear the colours, ask the levy in correct Legion phrasing. The bell rings on the hour.

name: Canal Reminder
notes: Pinned inside the door of a canal household at Riverwalk, in the householder's hand. The dossier fact is that ripper eels were trained to hunt Argonians crossing the canals unlawfully and do not attack anyone rubbed with eel-slime. The dossier places the trained eels at Lilmoth; the note does not name a city. The reviewer should confirm it need not.

name: Ferry Guide's Note
notes: A poler of the landing at Claywater Station, chalked on bark paper for passengers of the plank ferry. The guide chooses when to move and where to shelter, refuses to stop. Predators trail the boats; the passengers stand and balance. These are the dossier's account of guided river travel. The fare of 15 gold is from the ferry row in travel-services.json (ferry.imperial-fringe.drowning-gate); the dossier gives no fare.

name: Gang Roll
notes: The ledger of the gang that works the lower channel, in the hand of the overseers' clerk; the roll is read out at the camp, where the families know every name on it. The nushmeeko unit, the transferable, extendable and heritable Owing are dossier fact. Names and sums are particulars. The roll's reach beyond the camp is not stated.

name: Miregaunts of the Marsh
notes: Kratius Gray, a foreign naturalist writing for the Black Marsh Exploration Society. The copy lies in the held cargo at the North Cut Camp, taken from a walker and kept against claims. The dossier gives the creature, its materials, folklore and cavity; the lintel in a shoulder and the writer's first-person observations are his own voice. The dossier names him only as the author.

name: Stake-Ward Tally
notes: A grave-singer who tends and stakes the dead, writing at the Tag House where bones are handed over. Stakes carved with the whole story, pahnjee racks as a scent mask, the loose stake as a bog blight and the wet season testing the stakes are dossier fact. The count of 38 and 6 and the name Sha-Meeru are the writer's own particulars.

name: Station Water Ledger
notes: The well-keeper of Claywater Station, who keeps the counter, the beds and the stable. The cracking well, the failing Imperial stone, the landing's refusal to help and the double charge to travellers are the place record's pressures and quest hook (LF83). The figures are the keeper's own. Dates follow the calendar dossier: Rain's Hand is month 4.

name: The Three Mournings
notes: A primer written for the hatchlings of a village such as Nine Bends, where the gang families answer to the tree. The month meanings are dossier fact. The Second and Third Mournings' reasons are derived from shunatei in labour-and-bondage.md:58 because the dossier gives the months and not the reasons; the reviewer should judge them.

name: Toll Office Schedules
notes: The toll office at Cartwright's Cross publishes its schedules, as quest LQ15 requires. The column at the Broke Column copied them out and kept them with the pay book in the command tent. The Cross is a toll-road town on the Blackwood Road with a ferry. The days, hours and tolls are the notice's own particulars, not dossier fact.

name: Toll Tally
notes: The toll-holder of Riverwalk, at the post at the shore end of the plank walk. The record gives the toll on boats entering the pilgrim water, the rival claims of Thorn's field-owners and Hissmir's stewards. The post stands at the shore end of the plank walk. The boats, sums and the crew who paid neither are the toll-holder's own entries. The design file names the captain of Alten Corimont as a claimant; the catalogue record names Hissmir. The tally follows the record.
